verdict.v.title.unilateral_over: Eligible, but you’d overstay the limit
verdict.v.why.work: Working, studying or reporting in China falls outside every visa-free arrangement and needs the matching visa before you travel, regardless of length of stay.
verdict.v.why.passport: Visa-free entry applies only to holders of a valid ordinary passport. Travel documents and temporary or emergency certificates are not eligible under either the unilateral visa-free or the transit visa-free scheme.
verdict.v.why.unilateral: Under the unilateral visa-free policy (50 countries), holders of an ordinary passport may enter visa-free for business, tourism, family visits, exchange or transit, for a stay of no more than 30 days.
verdict.v.why.unilateral_over: {country} is indeed on the 50-country list — but visa-free entry allows no more than 30 days, and you plan {days} days. The excess does not work.
verdict.v.why.mutual: Under the mutual visa exemption agreement between China and {country}, holders of an ordinary passport may enter visa-free, generally for no more than 30 days.
verdict.v.why.mutual_over: The mutual agreement with {country} generally caps the stay at 30 days; you plan {days} days.
verdict.v.why.transit: You are a citizen of {country} and your itinerary is origin → China → a third country or region, which meets the 240-hour transit visa-free conditions.
verdict.v.why.transit_over: Your transit conditions hold, but the 240-hour scheme caps the stay at 10 days and you plan {days} days.
verdict.v.why.transit_not_met: The 240-hour scheme requires origin → China → a third country or region. Your destination is home / back the same way, so origin and destination are the same country — that is not transit.
verdict.v.why.hainan: As a citizen of {country} entering via a Hainan port open to foreigners, you may stay visa-free for up to 30 days within Hainan province.
verdict.v.why.visa_required: Under the conditions you selected, {country} does not qualify under the current unilateral visa-free, mutual agreement, 240-hour transit or Hainan schemes.
verdict.v.p.work.type: Visa type follows the purpose (Z work / X study / J journalist)
verdict.v.p.work.centre: Filed through a Chinese Visa Application Service Centre
verdict.v.p.pp.apply: Apply for the matching visa, or travel on a valid ordinary passport
verdict.v.p.uni.days: 30 days allowed; you plan {days} days — within the limit
verdict.v.p.uni.midnight: The stay counts from 00:00 the day after entry
verdict.v.p.uni.ports: Applies at all ports open to foreigners
verdict.v.p.uni.vs_transit: You also qualify for the 240-hour transit visa-free — but the unilateral scheme gives you 30 days. We compared: this one is better for you.
verdict.v.p.expiry.none: No fixed expiry date under the current arrangement
verdict.v.p.uni.evidence: Carry evidence matching your purpose (invitation, bookings)
verdict.v.p.uni.trim: Trim to 30 days or less → enter visa-free
verdict.v.p.uni.need_visa: Keep {days} days → you need a visa (L tourist / M business)
verdict.v.p.uni.leave30: The stay counts from the day after entry; you must leave by day 30
verdict.v.p.mutual.lists: Mutual agreements and the unilateral list are two separate lists — don’t mix them
verdict.v.p.mutual.official: Names and durations are subject to the latest official publication
verdict.v.p.tr.days: Up to 240 hours (10 days); you plan {days} days
verdict.v.p.tr.ticket: You must hold a connecting ticket with confirmed dates
verdict.v.p.tr.ports: Entry at any of 65 open ports across 24 provinces
verdict.v.p.tr.provinces: Travel is limited to the 24 covered provinces; cross-province travel allowed
verdict.v.p.tr.exclusions: Not available to those previously refused a Chinese visa or with illegal entry/exit records within 5 years
verdict.v.p.tr.visa: Need longer → a visa is required
verdict.v.p.trn.qualify: As a citizen of {country} you would qualify — but you must genuinely go on to a third country
verdict.v.p.trn.change: Change “leaving to” to a third country and recompute
verdict.v.p.trn.normal: Just a return trip to China → apply for a normal visa
verdict.v.p.hn.only: Travel is limited to Hainan only — if you also want Shanghai or Guangzhou, this route fails
verdict.v.p.vr.purpose: Choose the visa by purpose (L tourist / M business / Q family)
verdict.v.p.vr.centre: Filed via a Chinese Visa Application Service Centre; allow 4–6 weeks
verdict.v.p.vr.hainan: If you’re only going to Hainan and enter via Haikou or Sanya, Hainan’s 30-day visa-free applies
verdict.v.p.vr.transit: If your trip continues to a third country or region with a connecting ticket, consider the 240-hour transit visa-free
verdict.v.byline: Calculated by rules, not decided by AI. For preparation only; entry is subject to review by the competent authority.
verdict.v.blocked.title: Materials temporarily unavailable for assessment
verdict.v.blocked.why: Relevant rules have expired, await review or are not covered; no conclusion is provided for now. Check the original notices below.
verdict.v.blocked.point: No eligibility assessment before the materials are updated and checked.
verdict.v.review.title: Policy may have changed
verdict.v.review.why: Our source monitor detected a change and the rules have not been reviewed yet. The answer below is based on version {version}. Check the latest official notice before you book.

qa.a: Main-street safety in major Chinese cities is on the good side globally, and violent crime against tourists is rare. What actually catches visitors out isn’t danger — it’s scams.
li: Watch belongings in crowds — metro, shopping streets, park gates
Anyone approaching you near a sight to invite you to “tea”, an “exhibition” or a “jade shop”: decline flatly. It is the most common trap.
Disputes: call 110. No Chinese? Ask your hotel front desk to help.
qa.src: Basis: MPS public security guidance and travel advisories for major Chinese cities, 2026.

qa.q: Will my phone work? Google / WhatsApp?
qa.a: Phone and app availability depends on your device, operator, plan and network. Do not assume Google, WhatsApp or any other overseas app will work on every connection.
li: Ask your operator about international roaming, coverage, charges and SMS reception before travelling.
For a lawful local SIM or travel eSIM, confirm device compatibility, activation requirements and available services with the provider.
Save essential addresses, booking details and translation packs offline before departure.
qa.warn: Follow local laws and service terms. This guide does not provide instructions for bypassing network restrictions or guarantee access to overseas apps.
qa.src: Maintenance note: general connectivity preparation, not live network testing or a verified operator quotation. Confirm current terms and app availability with your provider.

qa.a: Language support varies by venue and staff. Before booking, ask your hotel, transport provider and attractions which languages and assistance they currently offer.
li: Confirm interpretation availability, booking requirements and any charges with the provider; do not assume a translation device is available.
Download offline translation packs and save your destination and hotel name and address in Chinese.
Show the written Chinese address when asking for directions; check key translations with the provider.
qa.src: General language preparation advice, not a verified inventory of devices or multilingual services. Confirm current support with each provider.

qa.q: How do I pay? Is cash still usable?
qa.a: Prepare more than one payment method and confirm availability before travelling. Card linking, identity checks and merchant acceptance depend on the provider and your account.
li: Ask each wallet provider which cards, documents and account setup steps it currently supports.
Ask merchants which payment methods they accept, and test your chosen method before relying on it.
Plan a cash backup and confirm nearby exchange or ATM services, opening hours, card acceptance and charges with the provider.
fees: Confirm platform fees, thresholds and any current exemptions in the provider's terms and payment screen.
Ask your issuing bank about foreign transaction, conversion and cash withdrawal charges.
tips: Check with your bank whether travel notification or additional authentication is needed.
Keep a backup payment method and the provider's support details; do not assume setup or payment will succeed.
qa.src: General payment preparation advice, not a verified fee schedule or acceptance guarantee. Confirm current terms with the wallet provider, merchant and issuing bank.

qa.a: Build a budget using quotes for your dates and itinerary. Flights, accommodation, transport, meals and activities vary by provider and booking conditions.
li: Confirm the total price, included services, deposits and cancellation terms before booking.
Ask the payment provider and your bank about platform and foreign transaction charges.
Check conversion rates, spreads and settlement currency before confirming payment.
tips: Compare final payable totals, not only advertised base prices.
Keep booking confirmations and the provider's written price and fee terms.
Set aside a contingency and do not assume a fee exemption or refund will apply.
qa.tail: For shopping refunds, ask the shop and refund provider about current conditions and charges. The Leaving screen provides reminders and reference estimates, not a guaranteed saving.
qa.src: General budgeting preparation, not verified prices or fees. Confirm current quotes and terms directly with providers.

qa.a: Check your passport, purpose, dates and full itinerary against the relevant official notice. A country list alone does not confirm eligibility. This tool covers selected routes only; missing coverage does not mean a visa is necessarily required.
li: Unilateral list: 50 countries, ordinary passports and listed purposes, up to 30 days. In this snapshot, 48 trials end on 2026-12-31, Russia on 2027-12-31; Brunei has no fixed end date, but still needs review.
240-hour transit list: 57 countries. Check onward travel to a third country or region, confirmed tickets, permitted ports and areas, document validity and all other conditions.
Hainan list: 61 countries, up to 30 days within Hainan. Do not treat this as nationwide travel permission.
Mutual agreements remain under country-by-country review. Non-ordinary documents and work, study or reporting need separate confirmation; this tool does not decide those cases.
qa.src: Controlled snapshot 2026-11-16: unilateral FAQ (2026-09-11), NIA Notice No. 4 of 2026 and visa-exemption guidance (2026-11-02). See the linked source documents; mutual agreements are not fully reviewed.

qa.q: Who do I call if something goes wrong?
qa.a: Save emergency contacts, your accommodation details and provider support information before travelling. Language support and service availability may vary.
li: Save 12367 for entry and stay enquiries; confirm current service scope and language support before relying on it.
110 / 120 / 119 — police / ambulance / fire; keep your location ready and ask nearby staff for language help if needed.
Save your consular contact details and confirm how to request help with lost documents or emergencies.

Before booking, ask the hotel to confirm check-in with your documents and accommodation registration. If there is a problem, ask the hotel or booking platform for alternatives; acceptance is not guaranteed.
qa.src: General help preparation, not a guarantee of language support or hotel acceptance. Confirm current services with the relevant provider.

dest.disclaimer: These themed ideas are for inspiration only. Reservation and ticketing details have not been individually tested; check with each venue before booking.

items.title: Great Wall, old capitals & the central axis
items.desc: A day on Beijing's central axis says more than any documentary.

booking.note: Real-name booking required. Passport holders can book online at most sites, but a few still need counter verification.

items.title: Water towns & classical gardens
items.desc: Suzhou's windows, Hangzhou's lake, Wuzhen's bridges. It only works slow.

booking.note: Popular gardens cap daily entries; book 3–7 days ahead in peak season.

items.title: Southwest landscapes
items.desc: Zhangjiajie's peaks, Jiuzhaigou's water, Guilin's river. Give this line time.

booking.note: Timed-entry tickets; passport number accepted at checkout on official channels.

items.title: Megacities & skylines
items.desc: Shanghai, Shenzhen, Guangzhou: easiest on English, easiest first stop.

booking.note: Most attractions take walk-ups; observation decks are worth pre-booking.

items.title: Worth a trip for the food alone
items.desc: Chengdu, Xi'an, Guangzhou. Menus are Chinese-only — which is exactly where AI earns its keep.

booking.note: Restaurants mostly don't take reservations for small parties.

items.title: Seasonal only
items.desc: Spring Festival lanterns, March cherry blossom, late-autumn ginkgo. Same route, different season, different trip.

booking.note: Peak-date slots sell out weeks ahead; check the exact bloom or festival window first.
